STAT 200.title: Elementary Statistics for Applications
STAT 200.description: Classical, nonparametric, and robust inferences about means, variances, and analysis of variance, using computers. Emphasis on problem formulation, assumptions, and interpretation. See the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion Lists:

children.raw: any course on the MATH_V 100 credit exclusion list

STAT 200.prerequisiteText: One of any course on the MATH_V 100 credit exclusion list [ MATH_V 190, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 100

STAT 201.title: Statistical Inference for Data Science
STAT 201.description: Classical and simulation-based techniques for estimation and hypothesis testing, including inference for means and proportions. Emphasis on case studies and real data sets, as well as reproducible and transparent workflows when writing computer scripts for analysis and reports.

STAT 203.title: Statistical Methods
STAT 203.description: Organizing, displaying and summarizing data. Inference estimation and testing for elementary probability models. Not for credit towards a B.Sc. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list within the Faculty of Science section in the Calendar.)

STAT 251.title: Introductory Probability and Statistics
STAT 251.description: Probability, discrete and continuous random variables, joint probability distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing, regression, analysis of variance. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list within the Faculty of Science section of the Calendar).
STAT 251.prerequisiteText: One of APSC_V 173, MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103

STAT 300.title: Intermediate Statistics for Applications
STAT 300.description: Further topics in statistical inference, including parametric and non-parametric methods, goodness-of-fit methods, analysis of variance and covariance, regression analysis, categorical data analysis, experimental designs, time series, model fitting, and statistical computing.
STAT 300.prerequisiteText: One of STAT_V 200, STAT_V 203, STAT_V 241, STAT_V 251, BIOL_V 300, BUSI_V 291, COMM_V 191, COMM_V 291, ECON_V 325, ECON_V 327, FRST_V 231, KIN_V 206, LFS_V 252, POLI_V 380, PSYC_V 218, PSYC_V 278, HES_O 340, POLI_O 400, STAT_O 121, STAT_O 121, STAT_O 205, STAT_O 230

STAT 301.title: Statistical Modelling for Data Science
STAT 301.description: Data analysis using statistical models and algorithms (e.g., linear and logistic regression, peeking, bandit, and variable selection algorithms) in case studies from different disciplines. Generative versus out-of-sample predictive models. Reproducible and transparent workflows for computer scripts and reports.
STAT 301.prerequisiteText: STAT_V 201 and one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, SCIE_V 001, MATH_O 100

STAT 302.title: Introduction to Probability
STAT 302.description: Basic notions of probability, random variables, expectation and conditional expectation, limit theorems. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list within the Faculty of Science section in the Calendar.)
STAT 302.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254, MATH_O 200

STAT 303.title: Introduction to Probabilistic Modelling and Simulation
STAT 303.description: Core concepts in probability taught through probabilistic generative modelling, simulation of random variables, basic Monte Carlo, common probability distributions and models, basic probabilistic model design and inference.
STAT 303.prerequisiteText: All of (a) one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001, (b) one of CPSC_V 103, CPSC_V 110, and (c) one of DSCI_V 100, ECON_V 325, STAT_V 200, STAT_V 251

STAT 305.title: Introduction to Statistical Inference
STAT 305.description: Review of probability theory. Sampling distribution theory, large sample theory and methods of estimation and hypothesis testing, including maximum likelihood estimation, likelihood ratio testing and confidence interval construction.

STAT 305.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of STAT_V 200, STAT_V 203, BIOL_V 300, STAT_V 251, COMM_V 291, ECON_V 325, FRST_V 231, PSYC_V 218, PSYC_V 366, PSYO_O 271, STAT_O 121, STAT_O 124, STAT_O 205, STAT_O 230 and one of MATH_V 302, STAT_V 302, STAT_O 203; or (b) DSCI_V 200 and STAT_V 201 and one of MATH_V 302, STAT_V 302, STAT_O 203; or (c) a score of 65% or higher in one of MATH_V 302, STAT_V 302, STAT_O 203. The Department recommends that students meet the prerequisite through option (a) or (b)

STAT 306.title: Finding Relationships in Data
STAT 306.description: Modelling a response (output) variable as a function of several explanatory (input) variables: multiple regression for a continuous response, logistic regression for a binary response, and log-linear models for count data. Finding low-dimensional structure: principal components analysis. Cluster analysis. (Consult the Credit Exclusion List within the Faculty of Science section in the Calendar).
STAT 306.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222 and one of STAT_V 200, STAT_V 241, STAT_V 251, STAT_V 300, BIOL_V 300, BUSI_V 291, COMM_V 191, COMM_V 291, ECON_V 325, ECON_V 327, FRST_V 231, PSYC_V 218, PSYC_V 278, PSYO_O 271, STAT_O 124, STAT_O 205, STAT_O 230 and one of MATH_V 302, STAT_V 302, STAT_O 203

STAT 321.title: Stochastic Signals and Systems
STAT 321.description: Stochastic behaviour of signals and systems (e.g., communication systems); discrete and continuous probability; random processes; modelling and identification of linear time-invariant systems; binary hypothesis testing and decision making.

children.raw: may be taken concurrently, with registration assistance from the Student Programs Coordinator in the Department of Statistics

STAT 321.prerequisiteText: One of ELEC 221, STAT 305. STAT 305 may be taken concurrently, with registration assistance from the Student Programs Coordinator in the Department of Statistics

STAT 335.title: Statistics in Quality Assurance
STAT 335.description: Philosophy of quality improvement and total quality control. Definitions of quality. Deming's principles, Ishikawa's tools, control charts, acceptance sampling, continuous improvement, quality design.
STAT 335.prerequisiteText: One of STAT 200, STAT 241, STAT 251, BIOL 300

STAT 344.title: Sample Surveys
STAT 344.description: Planning and practice of sample surveys. Random sampling, bias and variance, unequal probability sampling, systematic, multistage and stratified sampling, ratio and regression estimators, post-stratification, establishing a frame, pretesting, pilot studies, nonresponse and additional topics.
STAT 344.prerequisiteText: One of STAT 200, STAT 241, STAT 251, BIOL 300, COMM 291, ECON 325, ECON 327, FRST 231, PSYC 218, PSYC 278, PSYC 366

STAT 398.title: Co-operative Work Placement I
STAT 398.description: Work experience in an industrial research setting. Normally taken during Winter Session of third year. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Statistics.

prerequisite.raw: Registration in Statistics Honours or Major Program

STAT 398.prerequisiteText: Registration in Statistics Honours or Major Program

STAT 399.title: Co-operative Work Placement II
STAT 399.description: Work experience in an industrial research setting. Normally taken during Summer Session following third year. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Statistics.

STAT 404.title: Design and Analysis of Experiments
STAT 404.description: Theory and application of analysis of variance for standard experimental designs, including blocked, nested, factorial and split plot designs. Fixed and random effects, multiple comparisons, analysis of covariance. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list within the Faculty of Science section in the Calendar.)
STAT 404.prerequisiteText: STAT_V 305, one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, or MATH_V 223

STAT 405.title: Bayesian Statistics
STAT 405.description: Bayesian approaches to statistical inference: probabilistic modelling, Bayesian inference workflows, approximation of posterior distributions supported by modelling languages, analysis of Bayesian procedures and posterior approximation methods.
STAT 405.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 302, STAT_V 302, or MATH_V 418, and either STAT_V 305 or STAT_V 460

STAT 406.title: Methods for Statistical Learning
STAT 406.description: Flexible, data-adaptive methods for regression and classification models; regression smoothers; penalty methods; assessing accuracy of prediction; model selection; robustness; classification and regression trees; nearest-neighbour methods; neural networks; model averaging and ensembles; computational time and visualization for large data sets.
STAT 406.prerequisiteText: a) One of STAT_V 306, CPSC_V 340, or b) STAT_V 301 and one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223 and one of MATH_V 302, STAT_V 302

STAT 416.title: Advanced Linear Modelling
STAT 416.description: Advanced topics in linear modelling, including weighted least squares, model selection, robust methods, splines, Bayesian methods, mixed effects models, and generalized linear models.

STAT 443.title: Time Series and Forecasting
STAT 443.description: Trend and seasonality, autocorrelation, stationarity, stochastic models, exponential smoothing, Holt-Winters methods, Box-Jenkins approach, frequency domain analysis.
STAT 443.prerequisiteText: Both (a) one of MATH_V 302, MATH_V 318, STAT_V 302 and (b) one of ECON_V 326, ECON_V 328, STAT_V 300, STAT_V 301, STAT_V 306

STAT 445.title: Introduction to Exploratory Data Analysis
STAT 445.description: Methods for exploring and presenting the structure of data: one group of numbers, several groups, bivariate data, time series data and two-way tables. Data displays, outlier identification, transformations, resistant regression, several types of data smoothing, comparisons with standard statistical methods.

STAT 447.title: Special Topics in Statistics
STAT 447.description: Students should consult the Statistics Department for the particular topics offered in a given year.

STAT 449.title: Statistics Honours Project
STAT 449.description: A research project, undertaken under the supervision of a faculty member, resulting in a written report.

children.raw: Open to students enrolled in a Statistics Honours specialization and at class standing 4
Permission of the Undergraduate Advisor and supervising faculty member is required

STAT 449.prerequisiteText: Open to students enrolled in a Statistics Honours specialization and at class standing 4. Permission of the Undergraduate Advisor and supervising faculty member is required

STAT 450.title: Case Studies in Statistics
STAT 450.description: Readings and projects in areas of current statistical application including environmental science, industrial statistics, official statistics, actuarial statistics, and medical statistics.

STAT 460.title: Statistical Inference I
STAT 460.description: Statistical models and their properties, estimation methods, properties of point and interval estimation, likelihood, Bayesian inference. Intended for Honours students.
STAT 460.prerequisiteText: All of MATH 320, STAT 305 and one of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223

STAT 461.title: Statistical Inference II
STAT 461.description: Hypothesis testing and model selection in modern statistics, confidence regions, multiple testing, model comparison criteria. Intended for Honours students.

STAT 498.title: Co-operative Work Placement III
STAT 498.description: Work experience in an industrial research setting. Normally taken during Summer Session following fourth year. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Statistics.

STAT 499.title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
STAT 499.description: Work experience in an industrial research setting. Normally taken during Term 1 of Winter Session of fifth year. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Statistics.
